precedents.ratio_decidendi: Section 18 does not impose an absolute bar on the power of the courts to examine whether a prima facie case attracting the provisions of the 1989 Act is made out or not.; The bar under Section 18 only applies when a prima facie case is made out and the pre-arrest requirements under Section 41 CrPC are satisfied.; A prima facie case means that based on first impression, no offence is made out as shown in the FIR or complaint.; An offence under Section 3(1)(r) is not established merely by the victim's membership in a Scheduled Caste or Tribe unless there is intent to humiliate based on that membership.; The offence under Section 3(1)(u) applies only if enmity against members of the Scheduled Castes or Tribes as a group is promoted, not against individuals.; Mere knowledge of the complainant's caste is insufficient to attract Section 3(1)(r); intent linked to caste identity is required.; An insult under Section 3(1)(r) must be linked to caste identity and tied to notions of untouchability to constitute an offence.; Courts have the discretion to examine social media content alongside complaints to determine prima facie cases under the 1989 Act.
precedents.facts: The appellant, an editor of an online news channel, published a video on YouTube allegedly making derogatory statements and allegations against the complainant, a Member of the Kerala Legislative Assembly representing a Scheduled Caste reserved constituency. Offences under Section 3(1)(r) and 3(1)(u) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 were alleged. The appellant sought anticipatory bail, which was denied by the Special Judge and the High Court of Kerala, leading to this appeal before the Supreme Court of India.
precedents.usage_recommendation: The DEFENSE should use this precedent to argue that the absence of a prima facie case and the lack of criminal intent should lead to the grant of anticipatory bail. They can emphasize that the court has the discretion to examine the merits of the case before denying bail.
key_quotes: Section 18 does not impose an absolute bar on the power of the courts to examine whether a prima facie case attracting the provisions of the 1989 Act is made out or not.
distinguishing_factors: The input case involves IPC sections related to dowry and cruelty, while Shajan Skaria pertains to derogatory statements and caste identity, which may not directly correlate.
